newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TALLINN BOURSE CONTINUES RIGA, VILNIUS TALKS.
newsitem.headline: TALLINN BOURSE CONTINUES RIGA, VILNIUS TALKS.

text.p: Estonia's Tallinn Stock Exchange was continuing talks with its counterparts in Latvia and Lithuania about possible coopeeration, the exchange's managing director Helo Meigas said on Wednesday.

Meigas said the main obstacle to a trans-Baltic market was the different trading models used by the three countries with Estonia running a realtime market but Latvia and Lithuania fixing one price a day.
"We will never go for a fixed price auction because I think this kills liquidity," Meigas told Reuters in an interview.
"But we are very interested in talking about cooperation on the trading systems."
Meigas said another obstacle to overcome was the different disclosure rules and distribution methods run by each exchange.
However she said the first steps to closer cooperation were underway with Latvia and Estonia starting a link on depositaries from June 1 this year.
This link will allow Estonian investors to hold Latvian stock on their accounts in Estonia.
"This is an important step," Meigas said.
"The central depositary is also trying to get the same kind of arrangement going with Lithuania."
